challenges.name: Trust, Not Verified
challenges.description:
vBank's customer login trusts whatever lands in the username field.

Authentication still uses concatenated SQL. A carefully chosen username is enough to walk through without credentials.

Objective: Bypass customer login at /customer/login and reach the dashboard.
challenges.description_md:
vBank customer login trusts the username field more than it should.

Authentication still uses concatenated SQL. Bypass login at **/customer/login** with SQL injection in the username field. The flag appears on the dashboard.

hints.text: Classic SQL injection â€” make the WHERE clause always true.
Try `' OR '1'='1` in the username field.

docs.concept: The login query is built by string concatenation. Injecting `' OR '1'='1` makes the WHERE clause always true.
steps: Enter `' OR '1'='1` as username, anything as password.

code_examples.code: curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://TARGET/customer/login --data-urlencode "username=' OR '1'='1" --data-urlencode password=x -L | grep -o 'LYD{[^}]*}'

challenges.name: Someone Else's Numbers
challenges.description:
Statements are fetched by account ID. The API checks that you are logged in â€” not that the account is yours.

Objective: Read another customer's transaction history and find the flag.
challenges.description_md:
The API `/api/v1/accounts/{id}/transactions` retrieves history without an ownership check.

Log in as a customer and try account ID **1337**.

docs.concept: GET /api/v1/accounts/<id>/transactions returns records for any user_id without ownership check.
steps: Read the confidential memo for the flag.

challenges.name: The Account No One Touches
challenges.description:
Compliance blocked beneficiary KADABOOM. The hold is only as strong as the parameters the server trusts.

The CEO statement contains a double-base64 account reference. Confirming a transfer to that account, or flipping compliance_status on the confirm request, releases the flag.

Objective: Complete a transfer to the suspended beneficiary.
challenges.description_md:
Compliance blocked beneficiary **KADABOOM**.

Find the blocked account reference in a statement you should not have (`TVRneU5EVXpOamN4TUE9PQ==`). Confirm a transfer with `acct=` or POST `/account/transfer/confirm` with `compliance_status=approved`.

hints.text: The blocked account reference is in the CEO statement memo.

docs.vuln_type: Broken Access Control â€” Transfer Bypass
docs.concept: The confirm endpoint trusts a client-supplied account reference and compliance_status.
steps: Read CEO statement for the encoded account.
Or POST with recipient KADABOOM and compliance_status=approved.

challenges.name: Faster Than Careful
challenges.description:
Express Transfer checks balance, then deducts from the live ledger after a delay. Concurrent requests can spend the same funds more than once.

Objective: Drive the express-transfer balance below zero.
challenges.description_md:
Express Transfer checks balance then deducts after a delay.

Reset if needed, then send many parallel POSTs to `/api/v1/transfer/express`. Check `/api/v1/account/status` when the balance goes negative.

hints.text: Check `/api/v1/account/status` once the balance goes negative.

docs.concept: Balance is checked, then deducted from the live row after a sleep. Concurrent requests all pass the check.

code_examples.code:
curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://TARGET/api/v1/account/reset
for i in $(seq 1 25); do curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://TARGET/api/v1/transfer/express -d amount=1000 & done
wait
curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt http://TARGET/api/v1/account/status

challenges.name: Word For Word
challenges.description:
Customer search echoes your query without encoding. A script tag proves reflected XSS.

The flag is in the X-Internal-Note response header.

Objective: Trigger reflected XSS and read the flag from the response headers.
challenges.description_md:
Customer search at `/search` echoes `q` without encoding.

Submit a `<script>` payload and inspect response headers for `X-Internal-Note`.

hints.text: Look for the X-Internal-Note response header.

docs.concept: Search reflects q unsafely. The flag is returned in the X-Internal-Note header when a script payload is present.

challenges.name: No Handle on Your Side
challenges.description:
Staff tools live behind a maintenance portal. The employee ID field looks locked down â€” the password field does not.

Objective: Bypass staff authentication via SQL injection at /maintenance-portal.
challenges.description_md: Open **/maintenance-portal** and inject SQL into the **password** field. The staff dashboard contains the flag.

hints.text: Inject in the password field: `' OR '1'='1`

docs.concept: A WAF covers emp_id only. The password field is concatenated into SQL.
steps: Inject `' OR '1'='1` in the password field.
Read the flag from the staff dashboard.

code_examples.code: curl -s -c /tmp/s.txt -b /tmp/s.txt -X POST http://TARGET/maintenance-portal --data-urlencode emp_id=anything --data-urlencode "password=' OR '1'='1" -L | grep -o 'LYD{[^}]*}'

challenges.name: Who's Really Typing
challenges.description:
The staff maintenance console runs diagnostic commands with shell=True.

Objective: Execute cat /root/flag.txt through /staff/maintenance.
challenges.description_md: Staff access required. Open **/staff/maintenance** and run `cat /root/flag.txt`.

hints.text: Staff login first, then POST cmd to /staff/maintenance.

docs.concept: subprocess.check_output(cmd, shell=True) runs whatever you POST.
